top_choice_rationale: P001 (Buchwald and Hartwig, general palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling) is the only proposal where maturity, mechanism and credit are all settled. The bottleneck, slow C-N reductive elimination from amido-palladium complexes and competing beta-hydride elimination, is understood in elementary steps and solved by ligand design. The method has about three decades of independent reproduction and routine process-scale use, and the two-name allocation is clean. The 2010 overlap and the Kosugi/Migita 1983 precedent are handled by the words 'general' and 'development of' in the citation. P002 (targeted protein degradation) is scientifically strong, but no degrader is approved yet and the PROTAC versus cereblon glue credit boundary cannot be covered within three names, so I rank it second, ahead of no award.
